disaster_displacement.metric: new internal displacements during the year

timeline_events.title: Rohingya exodus consolidates in Cox's Bazar
timeline_events.detail: A year after the military crackdown in Rakhine State, roughly 745,000 Rohingya are registered in Bangladesh, forming the world's largest refugee settlement.

timeline_events.title: Venezuelan outflow passes 4 million
timeline_events.detail: Economic collapse and political crisis push the regional outflow past 4 million people, making Venezuela the second-largest displacement situation after Syria.

timeline_events.title: COVID-19 border closures
timeline_events.detail: 168 countries fully or partially close borders. Asylum registration stalls worldwide, suppressing recorded refugee numbers even as internal displacement keeps climbing.

timeline_events.title: Tigray conflict begins
timeline_events.detail: Fighting in northern Ethiopia displaces more than two million people internally within a year and pushes tens of thousands into eastern Sudan.

timeline_events.title: Kabul falls to the Taliban
timeline_events.detail: The government collapses on 15 August. Evacuations and renewed internal displacement follow, and Afghanistan ends the year as the third-largest origin country.

timeline_events.title: Full-scale invasion of Ukraine
timeline_events.detail: The fastest-growing refugee crisis since the Second World War. Roughly 8 million people leave Ukraine and a further 6 million are displaced inside it within the year.

timeline_events.title: Pakistan monsoon floods
timeline_events.detail: A third of the country floods. IDMC records around 8 million new internal displacements — the single largest disaster displacement event of the decade.

timeline_events.title: Türkiye–Syria earthquakes
timeline_events.detail: Twin magnitude 7.8 and 7.5 earthquakes displace some 3 million people across southern Türkiye and north-west Syria, many of them already-displaced Syrians.

timeline_events.title: War erupts in Sudan
timeline_events.detail: Fighting between the army and the Rapid Support Forces begins in Khartoum on 15 April, triggering what becomes the world's largest displacement crisis.

timeline_events.title: Gaza war begins
timeline_events.detail: Hostilities displace the overwhelming majority of Gaza's 2.2 million residents within weeks, most of them repeatedly.

timeline_events.title: Eastern DRC offensive
timeline_events.detail: M23 advances in North Kivu push DR Congo's internally displaced population past 7 million, among the highest ever recorded for a single country.

timeline_events.title: Israel–Hezbollah ceasefire
timeline_events.detail: A ceasefire on 27 November allows a large share of the roughly 1.2 million people displaced inside Lebanon to begin returning south.

timeline_events.title: Fall of the Assad government
timeline_events.detail: The government falls on 8 December. Hundreds of thousands of Syrians begin returning from Turkey, Lebanon and Jordan, the first sustained reversal in 13 years.
